newsitem.title: NORWAY: Egypt says Iraqi oil-for-food deal should go ahead.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says Iraqi oil-for-food deal should go ahead.

text.p: Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa called on Thursday for the immediate implementation of the United Nations oil-for-food deal with Iraq to end the suffering of ordinary Iraqi people.
"We call for the immediate implementation of the (U.N.) agreement and resolution pertaining to the oil-for-food deal," Moussa told a news conference in Oslo.
"The people of Iraq should not be further punished by the suspension of this agreement."
Moussa was on a two-day trip to the Norwegian capital to hold talks with Norwegian Foreign Minister Bjoern Tore Godal and Prime Minister Gro Harlem Brundtland.

The U.N.-brokered deal, which would allow Baghdad to sell up to $2 billion of oil over six months to pay for badly needed food and medicines, was put on hold on Sunday by U.N. Secretary General Boutro Boutros-Ghali.

Implementation of the plan had been expected in the next few weeks but Iraq's weekend attack on a Kurdish area in the north of the country and subsequent missile strikes by the United States at targets in the south of the country has heightened tensions in the region.

"We were concerned that the use of force in northern and southern Iraq would further exacerbate a situation that is already very critical," Moussa said. "The main concern now is to preserve the unity and foreign integrity and political independence of Iraq.

"The use of force has never solved any problem (whether it is) internal or international or regional. We call for a period of quiet where we can assess the events and help the people of Iraq move towards a more stable situation."
Iraq has been banned from international trade since its August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
At a regular meeting on Tuesday the U.N. Council made no change to the stiff economic sanctions on Baghdad.
